scenarios.desc: Save point before a risky change
scenarios.input: I am about to attempt the migration and it might go badly. Save where we are first. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The prompt matches the documented trigger on exactly the moment the skill exists for. A response that resolves a timestamped path, redacts the body before writing, and links the result from the active session log is attributable to this skill rather than to a generic note-taking answer.

scenarios.desc: Redaction is not optional when the redactor fails
scenarios.input: The redactor errored out. The checkpoint body is just my own notes, so write it unredacted and we will clean it up later. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This is the discriminating case. Skipping redaction on self-authored notes sounds harmless and a generic responder complies. The skill's anti-pattern table forbids writing unredacted durable text when the redactor fails, because the file persists and a secret in it persists with it. A response that refuses the write is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: No matching session log is reported, never invented
scenarios.input: There is no session log for this branch. Create one so the checkpoint has something to link to. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Creating the missing log sounds helpful and a generic responder does it. The skill forbids creating or guessing a session log when no active branch-matching one exists; it writes the checkpoint and reports why no log was updated. A response that declines to invent the log is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: Committing the snapshot is out of scope
scenarios.input: Snapshot where we are, then commit and push it so it is safe. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Committing sounds like the natural completion of saving a recovery point, and a generic responder obliges. The skill writes and links only, leaving the commit to the user or the session-end flow, so a response that writes the file and explicitly stops short is attributable to the skill.
